title: Understand a GitLab project
summary: A GitLab project contains a Git repository and related work tools. A group can organise several projects and their access in one place.
introduction: A GitLab project contains a Git repository and related work tools. A group can organise several projects and their access in one place. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A GitLab project contains a Git repository and related work tools. A group can organise several projects and their access in one place.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: These lessons use fictional examples and do not create or change any GitLab resources. Many public pages can be read without signing in. Writing to a real hosted project needs that service and suitable permission.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of GitLab. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Group: school-club
Project: reading-list
Repository: program files and Git history
Related tools: issues, merge requests and pipelines
blocks.title: Understand a GitLab project

blocks.text: The project is more than its files. Its related tools help track work and review changes around the repository.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain which part stores the code history.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: GitLab can be hosted in different ways, so a project is not always on gitlab.com.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
